PullRequest.Title: sessions: add per-item removal for recorded references and artifacts
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #336500.

Long-running Agents Window sessions accumulate GitHub issue/PR references (and other recorded artifacts) with no way to remove a single stale entry — only bulk copy/open actions exist today. This adds a per-row **remove** action to the session reference/artifact collections, reusing the existing session artifact-removal service by stable record ID, so a single entry can be dropped from the session's metadata without touching the underlying file, resource, GitHub issue, or pull request.

## Design rationale: removability is provenance-based, not kind-based

Per technical review, removability is **not** gated on whether an entry is presented as a "durable artifact" vs. an ordinary "reference", nor on its resource kind or which pill it renders in. Instead:

- Every persisted session record with a stable ID is removable **when its owning provider advertises removal support** — this now includes both `isArtifact: true` and `isArtifact: false` records, across file, resource, website, commit, issue, and pull-request kinds.
- Removal only deletes the session record. It never mutates the underlying file/resource, closes or edits a PR/issue, or removes an independent session association.
- Promoted GitHub issue/PR entries retain and use their own `recordedReferenceId` for removal — identity is never inferred from URL or title. Duplicate-looking entries (same URL, different recorded IDs) each stay independently removable.
- Git-/session-discovered issue/PR associations that were never recorded through `add_artifact_or_reference` have no recorded ID and remain **non-removable**. If a removed recorded entry also has an independently discovered association, that association can remain or reappear, and stays non-removable on its own.
- File diffs/changes are derived workspace/SCM state and stay non-removable — removal is never overloaded to mean revert/exclude/delete.
- Active browsers are live editors, not persisted records, and are intentionally out of scope for `removeSessionArtifact`.

## Behavior

- A discoverable remove action (❌) appears on every removable row, in both the collapsed single-reference chip's hover/menu and each row of an expanded collection dropdown.
- Removal invokes the provider's `removeSessionArtifact` operation with the entry's stable ID; the item stays visible until persistence succeeds, and only then is it removed from the UI.
- After a successful removal: the entry disappears, the collection's count updates, an emptied category pill (e.g. "Pull Requests") disappears entirely, and remaining rows/focus stay sensible.
- Failures are surfaced through the existing notification/error handling; the row is left in place so the user can retry — no optimistic success-shaped UI on a rejected removal.
- The remove action is a distinct control from the row's open/navigation action and does not trigger it.
- Removing an already-absent ID is idempotent; concurrent add/remove calls serialize against the latest collection.
- Copy, open, hover, and rich GitHub preview behavior (#335583) are unchanged, including keyboard navigation and Tab/Shift+Tab order.

## Screenshots

### Pull Request collection: rich row preview with remove action

![Pull Requests collection expanded, second row focused showing the merged PR's rich preview with Copy and Remove actions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be696221-6481-44b8-90af-21953ac331b5)

Focusing the second row surfaces the existing rich PR hover (branches, merge state) alongside the new per-row `Copy Pull Request URL` and `Remove Pull Request Reference from Session` actions.

### Issue collection: rich row preview with remove action

![Issues collection expanded, showing rich issue preview and per-row Copy/Remove actions next to the collapsed Pull Requests pill](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01fec5f2-0092-4bf6-b636-058ca6f06cb0)

### Removing the last item in a collection removes the pill

![Pull Requests pill fully gone after removing the only remaining PR, leaving just the Issues chip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aba126c0-edda-4dd0-82b9-c93668416516)

Removing the last pull request removes the entire "Pull Requests" pill — the count and category disappear together, rather than showing an empty "0 Pull Requests" pill.

### Single reference chip: remove action after keyboard-driven removal

![Single PR and issue chips after keyboard-driven removal collapsed each collection down to one entry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2a57c93-dd6b-4d3c-a0e0-f2b9a336a290)

Once a collection is down to one entry it collapses to a direct chip; hovering/focusing it still exposes `Copy … URL` next to the new `Remove … from Session` action.

### Persistence after reload

![Session reopened after reload, showing only the one reference that was not removed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aae885bd-7504-4d39-a50a-f452f7a71c9f)

Reopening the session after removal shows only the entries that were not removed — confirming removal persists in the Agent Host session metadata, not just the live UI state.

## Keyboard and screen-reader behavior

- The remove action is reachable via Tab from each row's other actions, in both forward and reverse (Shift+Tab) order, without disturbing the existing PR-branch/repository/ID control sequence from #335583.
- The action has an explicit, localized accessible name distinguishing it from a browser's `Close Browser` control (e.g. `Remove Pull Request Reference from Session`, `Remove Issue Reference from Session`) so screen readers announce the session-scoped, non-destructive nature of the action.
- Existing ARIA status/error announcements (e.g. from `sessionChatInputToolbar`) are reused for removal success/failure feedback.

## Implementation

- `sessionArtifacts.ts` (presentation layer): offers a `removeAction` for every `SessionArtifactKind` whenever the provider exposes remove capability, independent of `isArtifact`.
- `agentHostSessionArtifacts.ts` / `baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts`: promoted GitHub issue/PR entries now retain a per-entry `recordedReferenceId` (no longer deduped by URL across recorded entries), so duplicate-looking resources stay independently removable by identity; `createdByThisSession` semantics preserved separately from removability.
- `protocolServerHandler.ts`: the local Agent Host transport now advertises `vscode.removeSessionArtifact` support so `supportsRemoveArtifacts` is populated correctly for the local provider (this was previously gated off, silently hiding the new UI locally).
- `session.ts`: adds the `IRecordedGitHubReference` type carrying per-entry recorded identity.
- `chatDropdownPill.ts` / `chatPills.ts` / `sessionPullRequestPill.ts`: reuse existing row-action, icon, tooltip, and event-handling patterns from #335583 to wire up the new remove control without changing hover/preview rendering.
- `SESSIONS.md` / `AGENT_HOST_SESSIONS_PROVIDER.md`: documentation updated to describe `isArtifact` as presentation-only with respect to removability.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client` (test runner uses precompiled output)
- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean
- targeted ESLint on all touched files — clean
- `sessionArtifacts.test.ts` (browser/chat) — 10 passing, including new coverage for every artifact/reference kind and durable-artifact removal
- `sessionChatInputToolbar.test.ts` — 16 passing, including duplicate-URL recorded-PR removal and regression coverage for copy/open/hover
- `localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts` — 253 passing, including independently-discovered-association preservation after recorded removal
- `sessionArtifactRemoval.test.ts` (platform/node) — 8 passing, including idempotent removal of missing IDs and serialized concurrent add/remove
- `sessionArtifacts.test.ts` (platform/common) — 15 passing
- `protocolServerHandler.test.ts` — 149 passing, confirming the local capability-advertisement fix
- `actionList.test.ts` — 117 passing (no regression to keyboard/hover navigation from #335583)
- `sessionPullRequestPill.test.ts` — 6 passing, including dropdown-row and single-visible-PR removal coverage
- live verification against a real Agent Host session recording same-repository GitHub PR/issue references, exercising both dedicated collection dropdowns and collapsed single-reference chips, mouse and keyboard removal, empty-pill collapse, and persistence across a session reload

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed gate, metadata propagation, global all-session call path, concrete HTTP methods, recurring polling lifecycle, and concurrent scheduling are all directly traced. Exact user prevalence and reference counts are uncertain, which limits severity, but the mechanism and scaling are explicit.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub API requests and the retained polling/model objects for each distinct referenced pull request
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with the number of distinct ordinary GitHub pull-request references across all non-archived sessions. Identical coordinates share a model, but each distinct reference starts its own refresh and recurring poll; the session poller launches all distinct refreshes without awaiting or limiting them.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unbounded background GitHub request bursts and recurring network traffic can consume API quota, increase battery/CPU usage, and throttle live PR status updates.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The prior `if (!link || !artifact.isArtifact)` guard excluded `isArtifact: false` references from `IGitHubInfo`. They remained simple reference pills and never reached the global GitHub polling contribution; only produced PR artifacts and discovered session associations were refreshed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new `if (!link)` condition promotes every recorded GitHub reference into `IGitHubInfo`. `GitHubPollingContribution` tracks every non-archived session, iterates `getGitHubPullRequestRefs`, and calls `model.refresh()`/`startPolling()` for each identity. A PR refresh immediately issues pull-request and reviews requests in parallel, then open PRs add CI and review-thread refresh/polling.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The changed RIGHT line 121 replaces the old `if (!link || !artifact.isArtifact)` filter with `if (!link)`, directly moving all ordinary GitHub references onto the pre-existing global refresh/poll path.
Findings.Title: Keep ordinary references out of global PR polling
Findings.Impact: Opening/loading a profile with long-running sessions that accumulated many ordinary PR references now causes a concurrent GitHub API fan-out and keeps those references polling every minute even when their sessions are inactive. This can burn rate limits and create sustained background network work unrelated to the visible session.
Findings.Evidence: `partitionSessionArtifacts` now admits `isArtifact: false` GitHub records at line 121 and `toGitHubInfo` places them in `pullRequests`. The existing `GitHubPollingContribution` initializes trackers from all sessions, skips only archived sessions, maps every `getGitHubPullRequestRefs(gitHubInfo)` entry, and invokes `_pollPullRequest` in a loop. `_pollPullRequest` calls `model.refresh()` without awaiting; `GitHubPullRequestModel._refresh` performs `getPullRequest` and paginated `getReviews` via `Promise.all`, and open PRs additionally refresh/poll CI and review threads. Artifact collection cardinality is not capped.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the recorded ID for removal without globally polling ordinary references. For example, keep background polling limited to `getSessionOwnedGitHubPullRequestRefs`, and refresh non-owned recorded references only for the active/visible pill (deduplicated by GitHub coordinates and with a concurrency bound).

Scenarios.Scenario: Loading and background-monitoring non-archived Agent Host sessions that contain recorded GitHub pull-request references
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session metadata is partitioned into `IGitHubInfo`; the global GitHub polling contribution immediately acquires and refreshes every resulting PR model. This background work is not required to open the session UI, but it starts as soon as sessions are tracked and remains active for non-archived sessions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GitHub REST pull-request metadata GET plus paginated reviews GET; open PRs subsequently refresh CI and GraphQL review-thread data and poll them
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One model/request set per distinct owner/repository/PR number across tracked non-archived sessions after global model-key coalescing; ordinary references newly add to this effective cardinality. Each cold PR starts two parallel requests, with additional CI/thread requests for open PRs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: `isArtifact: false` recorded references were filtered before `IGitHubInfo`, so they stayed simple reference entries and did not reach the global PR refresh/poll loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs eagerly in the background and consumes network/API quota; it can contend with visible GitHub operations even though it is off the session-opening critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total distinct ordinary GitHub PR references accumulated across all non-archived sessions; the artifact collection has no cardinality cap.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Identical PR coordinates share a reference-counted model and polling scheduler, but distinct keys are iterated without awaiting and each `refresh()` starts two requests with `Promise.all`; there is no cross-key limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm consumers share models by GitHub coordinates and conditional ETags reduce payload/rate cost, but every distinct model remains scheduled at the recurring polling cadence. Duplicate record IDs for the same coordinate do not multiply network calls.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the changed provenance gate, propagation into `IGitHubInfo`, all-session poller, parallel HTTP methods, and polling lifecycle were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The repository does not establish a typical number of references per user, but the PR explicitly targets long-running sessions that accumulate them; exact latency/quota impact depends on that count and GitHub response times.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity boundary fan-out; finding submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering the active session's pull-request, issue, artifact, and reference pills and opening their dropdowns/hover actions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Section construction and pill rendering are synchronous UI work. PR data uses shared models already held by the global poller; issue refresh/polling starts only when the Issues pill is active. Dropdown row DOM/action creation occurs when the user opens or focuses the surface.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh and periodic poll of GitHub issue details
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared issue model per distinct GitHub issue coordinate in the active session; duplicate coordinates coalesce. Newly promoted ordinary issue references increase this count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Ordinary issue references were not promoted into `gitHubInfo`, so only issue artifacts reached this refresh path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial issue details are asynchronous and do not block basic pill construction; requests run when the issue surface is visible.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct GitHub issue/PR records and ordinary artifact/reference entries in the active session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Issue models are shared by coordinate; `refresh()` coalesces concurrent callers and debounces successful refreshes for 60 seconds, while one scheduler per model polls every 15 minutes. Distinct issue keys are not globally limited.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Issue models use reference sharing, a 100-entry snapshot LRU, ETags, and refresh debouncing. UI section arrays/actions are rebuilt reactively but retained only with the current observable derivation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the active issue request path and synchronous O(n) section construction; low risk for the added action-array allocations because they occur on normal reactive/hover paths and have bounded per-entry cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sessions may contain few issues in normal use; exact active-surface cardinality is unknown. This lower-frequency issue path shares the same provenance-gate root cause as the submitted PR polling finding and does not warrant a duplicate comment.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: network amplification is the same changed gate already reported, while UI allocation/rendering changes do not establish an independently material regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Removing one recorded artifact or reference from a session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The remove action awaits the provider request, session restoration, serialized mutation, and durable metadata persistence before the row disappears and success status is announced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: One `vscode/removeSessionArtifact` protocol request carrying the session URI and stable record ID
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one protocol call per user-invoked remove action; no per-row batch or retry fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Most newly removable rows had no UI action; existing supported artifact removal used the same provider operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the user-visible removal critical path by design; the UI waits for durable success.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore session state if necessary and persist the complete serialized remaining artifact/reference collection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One ordered durable write for a present ID; absent IDs skip persistence. Serialized bytes scale with remaining collection size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing artifact-removal service already performed this serialized full-collection persistence; the diff exposes it to more item kinds and local clients.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before the UI removes the item, preserving persistence/error semantics.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Size of the owning session's artifact/reference collection and user click frequency; there is no automatic bulk removal loop in the changed UI.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mutations are serialized per session with `SequencerByKey`; different sessions can proceed independently. A single click issues one request and no speculative parallel writes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No result cache is appropriate because each mutation must read latest state and persist it. Missing IDs are a no-op and do not write. Session restore may be warm for an active session.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: UI-to-provider-to-protocol-to-agent-service-to-persistence flow and per-session serialization were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large collections make full serialization/write cost larger, but removal is explicitly user-triggered and singular, and the diff does not increase boundary cardinality per action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: one awaited durable mutation per explicit action is bounded and preserves required ordering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Using hover and context-menu remove controls on single-item and dropdown pills
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hover options and context-menu action wrappers are created synchronously during hover/menu presentation; focus restoration runs after the action settles.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of currently rendered entries/actions, generally one pill or one opened dropdown at a time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No asynchronous work occurs until the user executes the wrapped remove action; that action follows the single serialized removal path above.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Hover/action arrays are ephemeral; existing hover content caches remain keyed by reference object. No new long-lived cache or unbounded retained collection was introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the synchronous call path; no forced layout, filesystem, IPC, or network boundary is introduced merely by opening the controls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact hover frequency is user-dependent, but allocations are small and bounded by visible actions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: added synchronous work is small, interaction-scoped, and does not establish rendering jank or retention.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 23 changed files and all diff pages. One concrete regression was reported: removing the artifact-only provenance gate moves every distinct ordinary GitHub PR reference onto the existing unbounded all-session refresh/poll path. Removal persistence, pill rendering, action promotion, focus restoration, and protocol capability changes were traced and did not yield additional independent performance findings.
